rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A concerns an unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepting 25MB bodies (yorkie-event.controller.ts / main.ts body limits); Finding B concerns using findUniqueOrThrow instead of an empty-data prisma.document.update in document.service.ts. Neither fix discharges the other.

panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25mb bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
panel.summary: Unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25MB bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
panel.evidence: `@SkipThrottle()` (yorkie-event.controller.ts:32) removes the only global rate limit (ThrottlerGuard registered as APP_GUARD in app.module.ts:113, 120 req/60s). The route needs no JWT/API key, so any client that can reach the backend port hits it. Express body-parser runs *before* guards, and main.ts:47-56 applies `limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT` (25MB default) to all JSON routes including this one, and additionally *retains* the raw buffer (`req.rawBody = buf`) only for this path — so each request pins the full 25MB buffer plus the parsed object until the guard rejects it, and the guard then computes an HMAC over those 25MB before rejecting. Attack: send many concurrent `POST /internal/yorkie/events` requests with 25MB JSON bodies and a garbage `X-Signature-256`; every request is fully buffered, doubled in memory, and HMAC'd with no rate limit → memory/CPU exhaustion of the backend. Nothing in the repo restricts the path at an ingress (no manifests present; the same process serves the public API on the same port). Mitigation would be a small per-route body limit (webhook payloads are a few hundred bytes) and/or a generous-but-finite throttle instead of a blanket skip.

coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts::consider using `finduniqueorthrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.summary: Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.evidence: **Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.** When `data` is empty, the current code calls `prisma.document.update({ data: {}, where })`. Prisma 6.6.0 may reject an empty `data` object at the client-validation level or generate invalid SQL (an `UPDATE` with no `SET` columns). The test mocks `prisma.document.update` so it wouldn't catch a real runtime failure. Returning the existing row via `findUniqueOrThrow` avoids the risk entirely and skips a needless write.
